source_message.text:
Hi Javed,

Thank you for the detailed introduction — your profile is exactly what we are looking for. Manual editing, the right tools, strong volume capacity, and a long term mindset. You checked every box.

Here is how we move forward:

We start every clipper with a first paid milestone — 3 clips. This is our standard onboarding process for everyone on the team regardless of experience. It is simply how we make sure we are aligned on style and brand standard before moving into the full contract.

What to do:
1\. Go through the YouTube channel and Instagram I will share with you
2\. Create 3 clips from that content
3\. Submit by Sunday

Once your clips are approved we will schedule a video call where I walk you through the full system — your daily task board, your payment dashboard where you can track earnings daily, your assigned Instagram account, and everything you need to hit the ground running.

Pay structure:
— $2.00 CPM per 1,000 views
— $600 maximum payout per clip
— Weekly and monthly performance bonuses

And to be direct — with your volume capacity and the leadership mindset you already showed in your message, the Lead Clipper path is very much on the table for you as you grow with us.

Confirm you are ready and I will send the links now.

value_updates.role_pathway: Lead Clipper advancement is available as the freelancer grows with the team.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Javed

First, I want to apologize for the delay in getting back to you. Even after we made our selections, a lot of the applicants we did not choose kept reaching out — some even offering to work for free just for a shot at this. I had to take the time to handle that properly and respectfully before turning my full attention to the five of you, the team we are actually moving forward with.

I also want to be upfront — a ticket will be created for you before the deadline so you are fully secured and paid on time. You do not need to worry about that.

Now, here is what's happening:

You are part of the first core team we are building. This is not just five hires — this is the founding group. As we move forward, top performers move onto our CPM based pay structure with bonuses. And from this group, one person will step into the Lead Clipper role — leading the team, approving clips, managing the other clippers, with a stable salary plus bonuses on top. That opportunity is open and it will be earned through consistency and results.

Here is what to do now:

Go to the Notion brand guidelines and read through everything carefully before you start — editing style, hooks, subtitles, what never to clip. Teyron's personal welcome video is being added there now along with example videos, so check back later today to hear directly from him and the vision behind all of this.

Once you've gone through the guidelines, start creating your clips. This is what moves you out of the Upwork trial phase and into the real system.

We are continuing to build out the Notion with more training resources, so keep checking back as those roll out.

Let's build this right. Excited to have the five of you locked in.

— Cleavon
Content Operations Manager, The Teyron Machine

value_updates.selection_model: One person from the first core team will earn the Lead Clipper role through consistency and results.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Javed,
Good work — you were the only clipper who finished before the deadline, and the quality backs that up. Moment capturing was on point, and the font choice worked well.
Two small things to adjust going forward:

One clip ran short — clips need to be 30-90 seconds to fully deliver the message/goal, so keep that range in mind.
No color on the captions/letters — adding color will help them pop more and improve watch time.

Neither of these is a big deal, just polish. Overall this was a strong first set and you're hired.
You'll receive payment for these clips on Monday. From there, you'll be onboarded properly with a better guideline video walking through exactly how we create a clip, the do's and don'ts, and what's expected.
One more thing — you're going to be the lead clipper for a pod of 6 clippers. That means you'll still be creating your own clips, but you'll also be approving clips from the other 5 and making sure the pod runs smoothly and everyone's hitting standard. I'll walk you through what that looks like before it kicks off, but wanted you to know now since it's a bigger responsibility than just clipping.
Congrats — talk soon.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Javed,

You are hired. Welcome to the team.

Before we go full speed I want to be straight with you about what this role actually requires — because I respect you enough to be honest from the start.

We are asking for **100 approved clips per month.** Not 100 submitted. Approved. I will be strict about the standard because the quality of every clip represents the brand. A clip that does not meet the standard gets sent back — it does not count until it is right.

That is the expectation and it will not change.

But here is my promise to you in return:

I will do everything on my end to make sure you have everything you need to hit that standard. I am recording new in depth videos specifically designed to show you exactly how to build a perfect clip — the pacing, the moment selection, the brand understanding, the editing style, everything. You will not be guessing. You will have full clarity on what we want and how to get there.

Because the goal is bigger than 100 clips. I am training you to become a **Lead Clipper** — someone who understands this brand deeply enough to approve other people's clips, lead a team, and earn up to $2,000 per month. That path starts now.

High standards on both sides. You deliver. I support. Together we build something real.

Contract is coming today or tomorrow. Stay ready.

Cleavon

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey team,

First, sorry for the delay lately. Upwork had us on hold and we couldn't move as fast as we wanted. That's sorted now, so we're back to full speed.

While we were on hold, I put together a new system to make your job easier and help you hit your 100 approved clips faster.

Here's what's new:

1\. Clip variations - you can now take the same body clip and change just the hook/opening to make a new version. You can reuse one clip up to 2-3 times this way. Less work, more clips.

2\. Shorter clip styles - these are quicker to make and easier to combine, so reaching 100 approved clips will be a lot smoother. Some of you could even push past 200 if you want.

3\. Hook training video - I'm making a video showing you how to find strong hooks. One long video can give you close to 50 clip ideas. This will make finding content faster and easier.

We see the work, loyalty, and commitment you've all put in, even with the delays on our end, and we appreciate it. This new system is to help you earn more without extra headaches.

Looking ahead, we want to build you up into Lead Clippers as we grow and bring more people onto the team. That starts with mastering this new approach.

More details and examples coming soon. Let's get back to it.

\- Cleavon

value_updates.role_scaling_model: Multiple current clippers may advance into Lead Clipper roles as the team grows.
value_updates.advancement_prerequisite: Master the new clip-variation, shorter-format, and hook-selection approach.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I had to end the contract. With tomorrow being the 1-month mark and only 1 clip delivered, despite me reaching out 3 times, I wasn't left with another option. This isn't personal — I just have to hold the same standard for everyone on the team, and the milestones exist for a reason.

I'm sorry it ended this way. If circumstances were different on your end, I get that life happens — but I need clippers I can count on to communicate, even if it's just to say "I'm behind" or "I need more time."

Wishing you well with whatever's next. If you ever want to try again down the line and things look different for you, the door's not permanently closed.
